Limits for investment in debt and sale of Credit Default Swaps by FPIs The limits for FPI investment in Government Securities (G-Secs), State Government Securities (SGSs) and corporate bonds shall remain unchanged at 6 per cent, 2 per cent and 15 per cent respectively, of the outstanding stocks of securities for 2026-27 for the General Route.

# Page 4^page=4
Limits for investment in debt and sale of Credit Default Swaps by FPIs The limits for FPI investment in Government Securities (G-Secs), State Government Securities (SGSs) and corporate bonds shall remain unchanged at 6 per cent, 2 per cent and 15 per cent respectively, of the outstanding stocks of securities for 2026-27 for the General Route. The allocation of incremental changes in the G-Sec limit (in absolute terms) over the two sub- categories – ‘General’ and ‘Long-term’ – has been retained at 50:50 for 2026-27. The entire increase in limits for SGSs (in absolute terms) has been added to the ‘General’ sub- category of SGSs.

# Page 5^page=5
The aggregate limit of the notional amount of Credit Default Swaps sold by FPIs shall be 5 per cent of the outstanding stock of corporate bonds. Accordingly, an additional limit of ₹3,30,464 crore is set out for 2026-27. Limits for investment in debt and sale of Credit Default Swaps by FPIs With effect from April 01, 2026, all existing and future investments under the Voluntary Retention Route shall be subject to the investment limits stipulated for FPI investments under the General Route.

Master Direction on Incentives and penal provisions for bank branches and CCs in respect of currency operations. RBI has formulated a Scheme of incentives to encourage banks for setting up requisite Currency Chest (CC) infrastructure and facilitating distribution / exchange of notes and coins. Further, the RBI has also prescribed a Scheme of penal interest/penalties in order to ensure accurate and timely reporting of CC transactions and provision of proper customer service to the members of public by CCs/branches/ATMs of banks.

Master Direction on Incentives and penal provisions for bank branches and CCs in respect of currency operations. RBI has formulated a Scheme of incentives to encourage banks for setting up requisite Currency Chest (CC) infrastructure and facilitating distribution / exchange of notes and coins. Further, the RBI has also prescribed a Scheme of penal interest/penalties in order to ensure accurate and timely reporting of CC transactions and provision of proper customer service to the members of public by CCs/branches/ATMs of banks. Why? In terms of the Preamble to and Section 45 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act) and Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, Reserve Bank of India issues guidelines / instructions for realising the objectives of Clean Note Policy and enhancing the efficiency of currency management operations.

# Page 9^page=9
Master Direction on Incentives and penal provisions for bank branches and CCs in respect of currency operations. Applicability - Scheme of incentives and Penalties mentioned in Chapter II and Chapter III will be applicable to all banks. Penal provisions for deficiency in operations of CCs will be applicable to all banks having CCs. These directions shall become effective on the day these are placed on the official website of the Reserve Bank

# Page 10^page=10
Scheme of Incentives The Scheme of incentives, for bank branches including CCs, based on performance in rendering customer service to the members of public has been formulated to encourage all the banks / bank branches to provide better customer service to the members of public keeping in view the objectives of Clean Note Policy.

Operational instructions on payment of performance-based incentive The incentive for distribution of coins shall be paid on the basis of net withdrawal from the CC. The CC holding banks shall raise invoice to RBI for claiming incentives. The CC branch shall pass on the incentive to the linked branches for the soiled notes deposited/ coins distributed/ mutilated notes adjudicated by them on pro-rata basis. The distribution of coins shall be verified by RBI Regional Offices through inspection of CCs/ incognito visit to branches, etc. The incentives in respect of bank notes shall be paid on the basis of: Soiled notes actually received in the Issue Office of the RBI Adjudicated notes received along with the SNR or sent separately by registered/ insured post in a sealed cover to the RBI.

Q1. Consider the following statements regarding Limits for investment in debt and sale of Credit Default Swaps by FPIs: 1. The aggregate limit of the notional amount of Credit Default Swaps sold by FPIs shall be 5% of the outstanding stock of corporate bonds. 2. Incremental increase in SGS limits is divided equally between General and Long-term categories. 3. SGS investment limits are capped at 2% of outstanding stock. Which of the above statements is/are correct? A. 1 and 2 only B. 2 and 3 only C. 1 and 3 only D. 3 only E. 1, 2 and 3 MCQs for Practice
